The Justice Department issued grand jury subpoenas
to Los Angeles County election workers.

The US economy picked up speed over the summer.

grew at an annual rate of 3.4% faster than it

But with inflation still high, NPR's Stephen Bassaz
says Americans aren't feeling it.
One of the first things I heard was disbelief

Part of the problem is that inflation is still high.

The new data comes from the last major government
report on the economy ahead of the midterm election.
President Trump will not be traveling

He had planned to hold rallies in those two states ahead
of midterm election day.

says he has opted to do telerallies instead
to reach more voters in some 20 states.
El Salvador has deployed more than 2,000 soldiers to Haiti
after four Salvadoran air techs were kidnapped.
NPR's Adar Peralta reports that the soldier's mission
is unclear.
In a statement written in Creole,
Salvador President Naibukkale says
his country is paying for the vast majority of the deployment
and that the planned operation is not an invasion.
He writes, quote, "The only thing we want
is for our four aviation technicians to come home.
The technicians were kidnapped almost two weeks ago.
One Haitian gang leader said they were killed by accident.
And the multinational force in the country
said they had received four badly charred bodies they
believed to be Salvadoran airmen."
Bukele rejected that claim.
The Haitian government says it welcomes the Salvadoran
deployment within the framework of a UN-approved gang
suppression force.
In his messages, Bukele seems to be
hinting at a broader operation.
Adar Peralta, NPR News, Mexico City.
This is NPR, an Australian woman who
murdered three of her estranged husband's relatives
by serving them beef wellington containing poisonous mushrooms,
has lost her appeal to overturn her convictions.
Erin Patterson had argued that she did not
receive a fair trial after being found guilty
by a jury in the Australian state of Victoria last year.
Adam Hancock sent this report from Sydney.
Erin Patterson had appealed her murder convictions
on a number of grounds, including a claim
that her case had been compromised
after the jury were housed at the same hotel
as members of the prosecution and a key witness.
But a panel of three judges dismissed her arguments,
claiming that they were insufficient for an appeal.
Instead, the judges agreed with claims from prosecutors
that Patterson's sentence was too lenient
after the 52-year-old was sentenced to life in prison
with a non-parole period of 33 years.
She will now be ineligible for parole
and will be resentenced at a later date.
Patterson has 28 days to decide if she wants
to take her case to the High Court of Australia.
For NPR News, I'm Adam Hancock in Sydney.
